messages:
incident-bot: 🚨 INCIDENT: Elevated 5xx + timeouts observed on /v1/generate. Paging oncall @sanjay. Gateways returning 502/504, spike started ~00:15 UTC. Automated alert: error_rate=12.4%, p95 latency=1.9s, p99=4.8s.

sanjay (oncall): I'm on it. Confirming which gateway cluster?

maria (sre): logs show gateway-a (us-west-2) fronting most traffic for this route. Batcher/scheduler queues growing on model-pool-3. queue_depth per pod: [120, 240, 180], avg queue wait ~850ms. Seeing head-of-line waits where 1 large request blocks batch.

liam (eng): stack traces point to a few long-running tokenizations from tenant:ai-playground. They sent a 50k token request that got through and is hogging the scheduler.

emma (support): got a ticket from AcmeCorp — they see errors in prod, "500 Internal Server Error" on LLM calls since 00:20 UTC. Escalation flagged.

maria (sre): digging into batcher metrics: batch_size distribution shifted left; continuous batching falling back to small batches because KV cache misses are causing cold-run slowdowns. Also kv-cache eviction counts spiked.

sanjay (oncall): immediate mitigation idea: 1) route ai-playground to a lower-priority lane / throttle their token rate. 2) enable fallback to quantized variant rdx-small for this route. 3) restart the busiest scheduler pod after draining. Any objections?

liam (eng): +1 for throttling noisy tenant. I can push a temporary routing rule. Command I'm going to run:```bash
# apply emergency throttling for tenant ai-playground
redwoodctl route update --tenant ai-playground --max-tokens-per-min 2000 --priority low
```

maria (sre): I'll prepare a restart play: drain connection on pod scheduler-3b using cordon+evict, then restart runtime. Doing drain now.

devops-bot: action: route-change queued by liam at 3799001251.

sanjay (oncall): also widen gateway fallback policy to allow rdx-small for 10% of traffic to reduce latency while we drain. liam, can you flip the canary?

liam (eng): canary flip command:```bash
redwoodctl rollout create --from model:rdx-medium --to model:rdx-small --route /v1/generate --percent 10 --reason "emergency surge fallback"
```

liam (eng): executed, canary started.

maria (sre): checkpoint: after throttling and canary, queue depth dropped on scheduler-3b from 240->60 in ~90s. p95 latency improving from 1.9s -> 720ms. Error rate now 6.1%.

emma (support): notified AcmeCorp via DM that we're investigating and applied temporary mitigations; asked them to retry. They're seeing some success on retries.

sanjay (oncall): rolling customer-impact note: partial failures for long-generation jobs and timeouts for some short calls that hit the hot queue. Marking SEV3 for tracking; possible SEV2 if errors don't fall under 15 min.

maria (sre): discovered root cause for the head-of-line: a single request with large system messages and a heavy tool-hook precompute that keeps the batch open for >3s. Scheduler FIFO causes subsequent small requests to wait for the batch to close. We're going to enable preemptive-eviction for oversized requests on the scheduler: set max_batch_hold_ms=600.

liam (eng): pushing runtime flag:```json
{"scheduler": {"max_batch_hold_ms": 600, "evict_large_requests": true}}
```

liam (eng): flag applied to pool model-pool-3.

maria (sre): after applying eviction knobs, I see batch close times drop; batch sizes normalize. queue depth stable. Error rate now 1.8%, p95 320ms.

sanjay (oncall): good. I'm going to hand off to @liam for postmortem and long-term fixes. Oncall shift ending in 30m — Liam will be primary. @maria can you collate logs and timeline please.

liam (eng): taking ownership. Next steps: identify why ai-playground allowed 50k token request (rate-limit policy gap), evaluate KV rehydration path, consider background warmup for large-model caches, add tenant isolation throttle defaults.

maria (sre): I'll export traces and attach the batcher traces to the ticket. Command:```bash
redwoodctl traces export --service scheduler --since 00:10 --until 00:40 --out /tmp/scheduler-traces.json
```

devops-bot: traces exported to /tmp/scheduler-traces.json by maria at 3799001284.

emma (support): AcmeCorp update: errors subsided after 00:26 UTC. They've asked for ETA on root cause. I've promised a follow-up and a postmortem within 24h.

sanjay (oncall): summary for incident channel: cause = noisy tenant large request + KV cold misses -> head-of-line blocking in batcher -> queue saturation -> gateway 5xx/timeouts. Mitigations = tenant throttling, canary fallback to rdx-small, restart busiest scheduler, lower max_batch_hold_ms. Impact = partial 5xx/timeouts across /v1/generate, few paying customers affected (AcmeCorp). Current status: stabilized.

liam (eng): logging this as INC-3799. I'll draft postmortem and action items: 1) tenant-level hard caps 2) default scheduler eviction for >X tokens 3) prewarm KV for large-model footprints 4) better observability for batch hold time.

maria (sre): final metrics at 3799001290: error_rate=0.9%, p95=310ms, queue_depth_avg=28. Closing live mitigation.

sanjay (oncall): thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
